To install line_profiler, use the command `$ pip install line_profiler`. For compatibility with IPython, use `$ pip install line_profiler[ipython]`. Ensure you are using Python 3.10 or newer. After installation, import `profile` in your relevant file(s) and decorate the functions you want to profile with `@profile`. Set the environment variable `LINE_PROFILE=1` and run your script as normal. Upon completion, a summary of profile results will be written to stdout.
To install `line_profiler`, use pip with the command `$ pip install line_profiler`. For ensuring compatibility with IPython, use `$ pip install line_profiler[ipython]`. The module requires Python 3.10 or newer. To use it, import `profile` in the relevant file(s) and decorate the functions you want to profile with `@profile`. Set the environment variable `LINE_PROFILE=1` and run your script as normal. The profiling results will be written to stdout when the script ends. The module is available under a BSD license.
To install line_profiler, you can download the source distribution from PyPI. The latest version available is 5.0.2, which includes files for various Python versions and platforms such as `line_profiler-5.0.2-cp314-cp314-musllinux_1_2_x86_64.whl`. If you're not sure which file to choose, you can learn more about installing packages on PyPI. The project description indicates that line_profiler profiles the time individual lines of code take to execute, implemented in C via Cython to reduce overhead. The script `kernprof.py` is also included for convenient profiling of Python applications and scripts.
```
$ pip install line_profiler 
```

Current releases require Python 3.10 or newer. Older Python versions require older `line_profiler` releases.
